title: ToolMatcher robustness harness for config/model shift detection
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Build a robustness evaluation harness that measures degradation in tool/function selection accuracy and argument validation fidelity when we change model variants, kernel/config flags, or quantization profiles. The harness should run as part of CI for critical rollouts and nightly to catch regressions that only appear under certain config permutations. Deliverables: (1) deterministic golden prompt set with expected tool selections and canonical args, (2) stochastic fuzzing suite to exercise edge-case args and schema violations, (3) delta-detector that computes per-config and per-model deltas for selection accuracy, argument schema violation rates, and downstream task breakages, (4) dashboard widgets and GitHub/CI gating logic to block or annotate rollouts. This ticket focuses on the core harness, end-to-end runner, and alerting integration; separate follow-ups will expand the prompt corpus and integrate with customer telemetry anonymization.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs in CI for model and config rollouts and in nightly pipelines
Produces per-change delta metrics: tool selection accuracy, top-1/top-3 precision, argument schema error rate
Delta detector raises regression alerts when accuracy drops >3% absolute or arg violation rate increases >1 percentage point (configurable)
Failed invocations captured with trace ID, model/config snapshot, and sanitized input/output for debugging
Dashboard in Redwood Console with per-config and per-model trendlines and a historical baseline view
A GitHub Action job that annotates PRs with regression status and can block merges on P0 regressions
Documentation with runbook for investigating common failure modes and recommended mitigations (fallback model, argument sanitizer, stricter schema)
implementation_steps: Assemble golden prompt corpus from existing toolcall logs + manual curation (privacy-sanitized)
Design JSON schema for expected tool arguments and canonicalization rules
Implement deterministic runner: replay prompts across model/config matrix and record selections and arg outputs
Add stochastic argument-fuzzing generator to exercise type coercion, truncation, and encoding edge cases
Metric computation: implement selection accuracy, top-k metrics, arg-schema-violation detector, and a composite regression score
Implement delta-detector service that compares baseline snapshot to candidate run and emits findings with diff summaries
Integrate with Redwood Console metrics pipeline and create dashboard widgets
Add GitHub Action and CI job templates that run candidate comparisons for PRs touching model/config changes
Write unit and integration tests and add test data to test harness storage
Roll out canary gating for a single internal team and collect feedback before wider enforcement
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Chen: Initial ticket filed after oncall report of argument-sanitizer regressions following runtime-1.21 rollout. Triage concluded we need a deterministic harness that also fuzzes args to catch brittle behaviors.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz: Sketched runner design. Decided on per-change snapshots and a composite score rather than single-metric gating to reduce false positives. Proposed default thresholds for P1: 3% selection delta, 1pp arg violation delta.

2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Reviewed scope; asked that the harness include a small set of explainability artifacts (attention traces + token alignments) for rapid debugging. Also requested exportable failure bundles for support cases.
2026-03-13 - Design review: Suggested UI states for the dashboard: baseline selection, candidate diff, failing example viewer. Design to contribute mockups in Confluence link above.

2026-03-14 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented deterministic runner core and basic metric aggregation. Pushed initial PR and added unit tests for schema validator. Next: integrate fuzzing generator and wire up delta-detector service. Blocking: need test harness storage allocation (ENG-214999) and a short-lived GPU quota increase for canary runs (ENG-215010).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict PR gating reduces production incidents but increases CI time. We prefer a tiered approach: annotate regressions for P2/P3 and block on P0/P1 only after triage.
Privacy: golden corpus must be sanitized. Work with legal to finalize redaction heuristics (follow-up task).
Long-term: integrate with customer-facing alerting and automated rollback policies in Dedicated/Private deployments.
